mainTopic: A lost כתובה, waiving a כתובה by words alone, and a new משנה on wedding preparation time and eating תרומה
overview: A woman lost her כתובה, and the couple asked רב יוסף what to do. At first he followed חכמים, who let a couple live together for a while without a written כתובה. אביי reminded him that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his גזירות, so רב יוסף told the husband to write a new כתובה. Next, the גמרא asks when a wife can give up part of her כתובה just by saying so. רב דימי and רבין bring opposite reports of what רבי יהושע בן לוי said about this. In both reports רבי יוחנן seems to disagree with him. Each time, רבי אבהו says that רבי יוחנן told him personally that they agree, and the words 'beginning' and 'end' are defined so the two fit. רב פפא says he would otherwise have made the two reports agree and let the two rabbis argue. The גמרא learns from this a rule: we prefer to explain a dispute as two rabbis using their own reasoning, not as a mix-up in reporting one teacher. Finally, a new משנה gives the bride and groom time to prepare for the wedding. It says when a betrothed woman may eat her husband's food and תרומה, and that a יבם does not let her eat תרומה. It then says these rules were the 'first משנה' and begins a later court's ruling, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A lost כתובה and רב יוסף's first answer
steps.stepSummary: A couple whose כתובה was lost comes to רב יוסף. He quotes שמואל: the strict rule is only רבי מאיר's view, and חכמים allow a couple to live 2-3 years without a written כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her כתובה got lost. They came to רב יוסף. He told them: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל that this strict rule is only רבי מאיר's opinion. But חכמים say a man may keep his wife for two or three years without a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A real case comes to רב יוסף, and he leans toward the lenient view of חכמים, so the couple would not need to rush to write a new כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a couple without a proper כתובה may not live together. רב יוסף, quoting שמואל, says this is only רבי מאיר's view. חכמים let a couple go on for a few years without the document, because the husband still owes her the כתובה money either way.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract that guarantees the wife's payment
Keeps / maintains (his wife, living with her)

phrases.english: Her marriage contract got lost.
They came before Rav Yosef.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: He said to them: This is what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
This is the opinion of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: "This" is רבי מאיר's strict rule that living together without a full כתובה is forbidden.

phrases.english: But the Sages say:
A man may keep his wife
two or three years without a marriage contract.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per שמואל, the ban on living without a כתובה is רבי מאיר's view; חכמים allow 2-3 years without one.

steps.title: אביי: the הלכה follows רבי מאיר's decrees
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף with another statement of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his גזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But didn't רב נחמן say in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his decrees?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back. He argues that רב יוסף should not rule like חכמים here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's rule about the כתובה is a rabbinic decree meant to protect the wife. שמואל himself said the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his decrees. So following חכמים here contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so... (a challenge opener)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Nachman say in the name of Shmuel:
The law follows Rabbi Meir in his decrees!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's lenient leaning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules like רבי מאיר in his decrees, and this rule is one of his decrees.

steps.title: רב יוסף agrees: write her a new כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף accepts אביי's point and tells the husband to write a new כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, go write her a new כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives in. The practical ruling is that the husband must write a new כתובה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not try to answer the challenge. He accepts that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר here. So the couple cannot rely on the lenient view of חכמים.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a couple may not live together without a valid כתובה. If it is lost, a new one must be written.

phrases.english: If so, go write her one.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is now speaking to the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's challenge
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The husband must write a new כתובה, following רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the dispute is only at the beginning
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי from בר קפרא, that the dispute over waiving part of a כתובה applies only at the beginning. At the end, everyone agrees she cannot waive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he reported from רבי שמעון בן פזי, from רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of בר קפרא: The argument is about the beginning. But at the end, everyone agrees she cannot give it up.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. It is about when the argument over a wife giving up part of her כתובה applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an earlier argument about whether a wife can give up part of her כתובה just by saying so. רבי יהושע בן לוי limits that argument to 'the beginning'. At 'the end', he says, all agree she cannot waive it. Steps 7-8 explain what 'beginning' and 'end' mean.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara:
The dispute is at the beginning,
phrases.notes: This is the argument over whether she can give up part of her כתובה just by saying so.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בַּסּוֹף — לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵינָהּ מוֹחֶלֶת.
phrases.english: but at the end, everyone agrees she cannot waive it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute about verbal waiver applies only at the beginning. At the end, all agree she cannot waive.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the dispute applies in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the dispute applies both at the beginning and at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: In both this case and that case, there is a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion is given, and it seems to disagree with רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי said everyone agrees at the end. רבי יוחנן says the dispute exists in both cases. So it looks like the two disagree about the end.

keyTerms.meaning: Both in this case and in that case

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Both in this case and in that case there is a dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seems to disagree with רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies both at the beginning and at the end.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: there is no real disagreement
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports that רבי יוחנן personally told him that he and רבי יהושע בן לוי do not disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: רבי יוחנן himself explained to me that he and רבי יהושע בן לוי do not argue with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It announces that the two opinions really agree, and the explanation comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו heard this directly from רבי יוחנן, so it is reliable. The claim is that the difference is only in wording, not in the actual law.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally
We do not argue with each other

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: It was explained to me personally by Rabbi Yochanan
that I and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
phrases.notes: "I" here is רבי יוחנן, quoted by רבי אבהו.

phrases.english: do not disagree with one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent conflict between steps 4 and 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: the difference is only in wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree about the end.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree; they just mean different things by 'beginning' and 'end'.

steps.title: What רבי יהושע בן לוי meant by 'beginning' and 'end'
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהושע בן לוי, 'beginning' means the start of the חופה, and 'end' means after the ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did רבי יהושע בן לוי mean by 'the beginning'? The start of the חופה. And what is 'the end'? After the ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the terms of רבי יהושע בן לוי, so we can see that the two match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's 'end' is after the marriage has been completed through ביאה. Only from that point does everyone agree that she cannot waive by words alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of the חופה (wedding ceremony)
After the marriage has been completed through relations

phrases.aramaic: מַאי ״בַּתְּחִלָּה״ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי —
phrases.english: What is 'at the beginning' that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said?
The beginning of the wedding ceremony.
And what is 'the end'? The end of intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״בַּתְּחִלָּה״ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Beginning' means the start of the חופה; 'end' means after ביאה.

steps.title: What רבי יוחנן meant by 'both cases'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's 'both cases' means the start of the חופה and the end of the חופה, which is the start of the ביאה. So both rabbis agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when I said 'both in this case and that case there is a dispute', I meant the start of the חופה and the end of the חופה, which is the start of the ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains his own words, and this shows that he and רבי יהושע בן לוי hold the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of רבי יוחנן's cases happen before the ביאה. Both rabbis agree that the dispute runs until the marriage is completed through ביאה. After that, everyone agrees she cannot waive by words alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of the time for relations

steps.whatToRemember: In רב דימי's version, both רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן agree: the dispute about giving up part of a כתובה by words alone applies only until the ביאה. After that, all agree she cannot waive it verbally. (רבין's version, in steps 9-13, reports it differently.)
steps.confusionAlert: Both rabbis use the word 'end' (סוף), but they mean different points in time. For רבי יהושע בן לוי, it is after the ביאה. For רבי יוחנן, it is the end of the חופה, before the ביאה.

phrases.english: And when I said
'both in this case and in that case there is a dispute,'
I meant the beginning of the wedding ceremony and the end of the wedding ceremony,
which is the beginning of intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי קָאָמֵינָא אֲנָא בֵּין בָּזוֹ וּבֵין בָּזוֹ מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the harmonization begun in step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רב דימי's version, there is no real disagreement. The dispute applies only until the ביאה; after it, all agree there is no verbal waiver.

steps.title: רבין brings the opposite version
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the מחלוקת is only at the end, and at the beginning everyone agrees she can waive.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said: רבי שמעון בן פזי said that רבי יהושע בן לוי said in the name of בר קפרא: the argument is only at the end. But at the beginning, everyone agrees she can waive.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report arrives, from רבין, about what רבי יהושע בן לוי said. It is the reverse of רב דימי's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי said the מחלוקת is at the beginning, and at the end everyone agrees she cannot waive. רבין flips it: the מחלוקת is at the end, and at the beginning everyone agrees she can waive. Now we have two reports that seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: When [he] came. Used when a scholar arrives in בבל from ארץ ישראל with a teaching.
An אמורא who carried teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל, like רב דימי.
She can waive (give up her right)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two reports. רב דימי: argument at the beginning, at the end she can NOT waive. רבין: argument at the end, at the beginning she CAN waive.

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of Bar Kappara:
The dispute is at the end,
phrases.notes: The dispute about whether she can give up part of her כתובה just by saying so.

phrases.english: but at the beginning
everyone agrees she can waive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second, opposite report of רבי יהושע בן לוי's position, alongside רב דימי's report in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבין, the מחלוקת is only at the end; at the beginning all agree she can verbally waive.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the dispute is in both cases
steps.stepSummary: In רבין's report, רבי יוחנן says the מחלוקת applies both at the beginning and at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: in both this case and that case, there is an argument.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין's report continues with רבי יוחנן's view: the argument applies at both points in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי limited the argument to the end only. רבי יוחנן seems to disagree, saying the argument applies at both times. So it looks like the two rabbis argue again.

keyTerms.meaning: Both in this one and in that one
The leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
And [so-and-so] said. Here it brings a second, seemingly different view.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Both in this case and in that case there is a dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents רבי יוחנן's seemingly opposing view within רבין's report.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the מחלוקת applies both at the beginning and at the end.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: רבי יוחנן said they do not argue
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports that רבי יוחנן told him personally that he and רבי יהושע בן לוי do not disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: רבי יוחנן himself explained it to me: I and רבי יהושע בן לוי do not argue with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like in רב דימי's version, רבי אבהו steps in and says the two rabbis really agree. He is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It looked like רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. רבי אבהו heard directly from רבי יוחנן that they do not. Next, he will show how their words fit together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
To me personally it was explained
by Rabbi Yochanan himself,
that I and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
do not disagree with one another:

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent conflict between steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both opinions are about different moments in time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue about when the מחלוקת applies.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not argue; they are talking about different points in time.

steps.title: What רבי יהושע בן לוי meant
steps.stepSummary: In רבין's version, 'end' means the end of the חופה, and 'beginning' means the start of the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'end' that רבי יהושע בן לוי said? The end of the חופה. And what is the 'beginning'? The start of the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defines the words 'beginning' and 'end' in רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both times are about the חופה. At the start of the חופה, everyone agrees she can waive. At the end of the חופה, the מחלוקת applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The wedding canopy, the stage that completes the marriage

phrases.english: What is "at the end"
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said?
The end of the wedding ceremony.
And what is "beginning"?
The beginning of the wedding ceremony.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״לְבַסּוֹף״ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins carrying out the harmonization promised in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יהושע בן לוי, per רבין: beginning = start of חופה, end = end of חופה.

steps.title: What רבי יוחנן meant by 'both'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's 'both cases' means the start of ביאה and the end of ביאה, so the two rabbis do not argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when I said 'in both cases there is an argument', I meant the start of ביאה and the end of ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains that his 'both' was about two different moments, so he does not contradict רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the חופה is the same moment as the start of ביאה. So both rabbis agree there is a מחלוקת from that moment on. רבי יוחנן's wording makes clear that the argument continues even after ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations, which complete the marriage
The start of the time for ביאה

steps.whatToRemember: In רבין's version: at the start of the חופה everyone agrees she can waive. From the end of the חופה (the start of ביאה) and on, there is a מחלוקת, and רבי יוחנן says it continues even after ביאה.

phrases.english: And when I said
that both in this and in that there is a dispute,
I meant the beginning of intercourse and the end of intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי קָאָמֵינָא אֲנָא בֵּין בָּזוֹ בֵּין בָּזוֹ מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the harmonization by defining רבי יוחנן's terms.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Per רבין, רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי agree; they speak about different moments in time.

steps.title: רב פפא: how I would have read it otherwise
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that without רבי אבהו's report, he would have said רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue, while רב דימי and רבין agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: if not for רבי אבהו's report that רבי יוחנן said 'I and רבי יהושע בן לוי do not argue', I would have said that רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי do argue, and רב דימי and רבין do not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a different way he would have lined up the opinions. He sets up an explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, the גמרא made the two rabbis agree in each report. רב פפא would have done the opposite: make the two reports (רב דימי and רבין) agree, and let the two rabbis argue. He only drops this because רבי אבהו heard otherwise from רבי יוחנן himself.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If not that Rabbi Abbahu said
"To me personally it was explained
by Rabbi Yochanan himself
that I and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
do not disagree with one another,"
I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree,
while Rav Dimi and Ravin do not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an alternative way to line up all the opinions, which רבי אבהו's report rules out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא's hypothetical reading: the two reports match, and רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue.

steps.title: How רב דימי and רבין would match
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains: רבין's 'end' means end of the חופה, and רב דימי's 'beginning' means start of ביאה, which is the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'end' that רבין said? The end of the חופה. And what is the 'beginning' that רב דימי said? The start of ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא shows how the two reports would say the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the חופה and the start of ביאה are the same moment. So both reports would put the מחלוקת at that exact time. Before it, all agree she can waive (רבין); after ביאה, all agree she cannot (רב דימי).

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who, like רבין, brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל

phrases.english: What is the "end" that Ravin said?
The end of the wedding ceremony.
And what is the "beginning" that Rav Dimi said?
The beginning of intercourse.
phrases.notes: This starts right when the חופה ends, so it is the same moment as רבין's "end."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in how רב פפא's hypothetical reading makes רב דימי and רבין agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב פפא's reading, both reports place the מחלוקת at the end of the חופה, which is the start of ביאה.

steps.title: What is רב פפא teaching us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what point there is in רב פפא's statement, since he admits רבי אבהו's report rules it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא bothered to share a reading that he himself says is wrong. This sets up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא accepts that רבי יוחנן said he does not argue with רבי יהושע בן לוי. So his other reading is not the right one. The גמרא wants to know what practical lesson his words still hold.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? What new point does he make?

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of רב פפא's hypothetical reading in steps 14 and 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רב פפא's rejected reading still teaches.

steps.title: The point of רב פפא's statement: prefer a dispute over reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא teaches that it is better to say two אמוראים argue over their own logic than to say two reporters disagree about what one teacher said.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: we prefer to say that two אמוראים argue about their own reasoning. We do not prefer to say that two אמוראים argue about what one other אמורא held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from step 16 and explains why רב פפא's statement is still useful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רבי אבהו's report, רב פפא would have said that רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי truly disagree, while רב דימי and רבין agree. His reason is a general rule. A real disagreement in logic is more likely than two students passing on one teacher's words differently.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: A general rule: when we have a choice, we explain a dispute as two אמוראים each with their own reasoning, not as a mix-up in reporting one teacher's words.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule closes the whole discussion about the reports of רב דימי and רבין, and it guides how we read reported disputes in general.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that two אמוראים argue
about their own reasoning,
and two אמוראים do not argue
about the view of one אמורא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא's point is a general rule: we prefer to say there is a dispute in reasoning, not a dispute about what one teacher said.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Prefer to explain a dispute as two independent opinions, not as conflicting reports of one teacher.

steps.title: How long the bride and groom get to prepare for the wedding
steps.stepSummary: A virgin gets twelve months after the husband asks to marry her, a man gets the same, and a widow gets thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: We give a virgin twelve months from the time the husband asks to marry her, so she can prepare herself. Just as we give the woman time, we also give the man time to prepare himself. A widow gets thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets how much time each side gets to get ready between אירוסין and the wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clock starts when the husband asks to finish the marriage, not at the אירוסין itself. The man also needs time, so he gets the same amount. A widow gets much less time.

keyTerms.meaning: A virgin, a woman marrying for the first time
He asked for her, meaning he asked to finish the marriage
To prepare herself, with clothing and jewelry

steps.confusionAlert: The twelve months start when the husband asks to marry her, not on the day of the אירוסין.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
We give a virgin twelve months
from when the husband asked for her,
phrases.notes: He already did אירוסין with her, and now he asks to finish the marriage.

phrases.english: to prepare herself.
And just as we give the woman time,
so too we give the man time
to prepare himself.
And to a widow, thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נוֹתְנִין לַבְּתוּלָה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A virgin and the man each get twelve months to prepare. A widow gets thirty days.

steps.title: When the time passes without a wedding, she eats from his food
steps.stepSummary: If the set time passed and they did not marry, he must feed her, and if he is a כהן she may eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the set time arrived and they did not get married, the women eat from his food and they may eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules what happens once the preparation time is over and the wedding still has not taken place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the time is up, she is treated in some ways like a married wife. He must support her. If he is a כהן, she may even eat תרומה, though she is still only betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: They got married, meaning the חופה
From his, meaning from the husband's food
The portion of produce given to a כהן; only a כהן and his household may eat it

phrases.english: If the time arrived and they did not get married,
they eat from his food,
phrases.notes: "They" means the women, both the virgin and the widow.

phrases.english: and they eat תרומה.
phrases.notes: This is when the husband is a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States what happens once the time set in step 18 has passed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the set time, the husband supports her, and if he is a כהן she may eat תרומה.

steps.title: רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא: how much of her food may be תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון says he may give her all her food as תרומה. רבי עקיבא says half must be regular food and half may be תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: he may give her all of it as תרומה. רבי עקיבא says: half regular food and half תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two תנאים argue about how the כהן may give food to his betrothed wife once the time is up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree she may eat תרומה. They only argue whether all her food may be תרומה, or whether half must be חולין. The משנה does not give the reasons here.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, a Sage of the משנה
A תנא, a Sage of the משנה
Regular food that is not holy

phrases.english: רבי טרפון says:
He may give her all of it as תרומה.
רבי עקיבא says:
Half regular food and half תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: נוֹתְנִין לָהּ הַכֹּל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues about how the rule of step 19 is carried out
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: all may be תרומה. רבי עקיבא: half חולין, half תרומה.

steps.title: A יבם does not let her eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A woman waiting for her יבם may not eat תרומה because of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The יבם does not let her eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule: the link to a יבם who is a כהן does not allow the widow to eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a husband, the betrothal plus the passing of the time allows תרומה. A יבם is different. Even if he is a כהן, his tie to her does not give her this right.

keyTerms.meaning: The brother of a man who died without children, who is meant to marry the widow
Lets someone eat, gives the right to eat

phrases.english: The יבם does not let her eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the תרומה rule of step 19: it does not apply with a יבם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבם who is a כהן does not allow the woman to eat תרומה.

steps.title: Time with the husband and the יבם does not add up
steps.stepSummary: If the twelve months were split between the husband and the יבם, even with only one day on one side, she still may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she spent six months waiting for the husband and six months waiting for the יבם, or even all of it with the husband except one day with the יבם, or all of it with the יבם except one day with the husband, she does not eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the יבם rule to cases where the waiting time was split between the husband and the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiting time under the husband and the time under the יבם cannot be added together. Even one day under the other person breaks it. So she never completed a full period under one man who can give her תרומה.
steps.whatToRemember: Time under the husband and time under the יבם never add up for תרומה, not even when only one day is missing.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that almost all the time with the husband is enough. Even one day under the יבם means she may not eat תרומה.

phrases.english: If she spent six months waiting for the husband,
and six months waiting for the יבם,
or even all of them waiting for the husband
except one day waiting for the יבם,
or all of them waiting for the יבם
except one day waiting for the husband,
she does not eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשְׂתָה שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים בִּפְנֵי הַבַּעַל וְשִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים בִּפְנֵי הַיָּבָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the יבם rule of step 21 to split waiting periods
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If any part of the twelve months was under the יבם, she may not eat תרומה.

steps.title: The earlier rulings were the original version, and a later court is about to change them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the rules just taught about eating תרומה were the 'first משנה'. Then it begins to tell us what a later בית דין ruled instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the first version of the משנה. A court that came after them said:
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה labels the rulings it just gave as the older, original version of the law. Then it opens the door to a newer ruling from a later בית דין. The second half is a setup line; the actual new ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything from Steps 19-22 about the engaged woman eating תרומה was the older ruling, called משנה ראשונה. The words 'a court after them said' tell us the law was later changed. So we should not treat the earlier rulings as the final law until we hear what the later בית דין said.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'first משנה': the earlier, original version of a ruling that was later changed
A Jewish court of rabbis that rules on the law
That came after them, from a later time
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which only a כהן and his household may eat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at Steps 19-22 and think that is the final law. The משנה is telling you those rulings were the older version, and a later court changed them.
steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase משנה ראשונה is a signal that the law changed over time. Whenever you see it, look for the newer ruling that follows, because that one is usually the one that counts.

phrases.english: This is the first version of the משנה.
phrases.notes: 'This' points back to the rulings we just learned about the engaged woman eating תרומה.

phrases.english: A court that came after them said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back on Steps 19-22, calls them the older version of the law, and begins to introduce a later court's different ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rulings allowing an engaged woman to eat תרומה once the wedding time has passed are the older version, called משנה ראשונה. A later בית דין ruled differently, and that ruling follows.
